title: Substrate: the machine under the interpreter

atom_notes.A13: most substrate findings are side channels or timing oracles
atom_notes.A07: memory pressure and pause behaviour are resource boundaries
atom_notes.A05: type confusion between the engine's view and the hardware's

required_cells.why: you cannot measure a machine you have not characterised
proving a side channel needs statistics, not a single reading

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Clock resolution and coarsening
entries.role: What a page can actually measure. If the clock is quantised to 100 microseconds or jittered, a side channel needs a different technique, and the difference is measurable rather than assumed.
preconditions: a page context able to read a high resolution timer
a host where isolation settings can be varied
oracle: the observed granularity step, measured across many reads
the same step changing when isolation or site isolation settings change
a jitter distribution wider than the value being inferred, which ends the technique

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: JIT tier thresholds and deopt behaviour
entries.role: Where the interpreter stops and the optimiser starts, and what assumption invalidates it. Tier thresholds are the reason a payload behaves differently on iteration 9000 than on iteration 10.
preconditions: a script context that can time its own function calls
oracle: a discontinuity in per call latency at a specific iteration count, repeatable
a deopt storm visible as a latency step when the argument type changes mid loop

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: WebAssembly compilation and memory growth
entries.role: How a module is compiled relative to JavaScript, and what happens to views held across a memory growth. A detached buffer is the observable that most callers forget.
preconditions: the page can instantiate a WebAssembly module
oracle: tier up timing of a wasm function against its JavaScript twin
an ArrayBuffer view detached after memory.grow, observed rather than documented

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Allocator size classes and reuse order
entries.role: Which allocations land in the same region and what a freed chunk becomes. Heap grooming is impossible without this, and most of it is observable from script through allocation timing.
preconditions: a script context with allocation primitives
a build with the target allocator
oracle: objects of chosen sizes landing in adjacent regions, inferred from access timing
LIFO or FIFO reuse shown by address ordering after a controlled free sequence
a quarantine delay detected as a gap between free and reuse

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Collector movement, finalizers and pause shape
entries.role: Whether live objects move, when finalizers run relative to death, and whether a pause is long enough to be an oracle. Moving collectors decide whether a stale reference corrupts or merely fails.
preconditions: allocation pressure can be induced from script
oracle: address stability across a forced collection
finalizer output ordered against a sentinel
pause distribution measured against a fixed workload

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Sandbox reach and descriptor inheritance
entries.role: What a compromised renderer can reach. The policy, the reachable descriptors and the broker interface decide whether a renderer bug is a browser bug or a host bug.
preconditions: a renderer process to inspect on a host where it can be observed
oracle: the seccomp policy and the open descriptor table, enumerated
a syscall refused at the policy and a neighbouring one permitted
a descriptor inherited into a helper that should not hold it

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Native parser reachability from a page
entries.role: Which native decoders a page can feed on purpose. Fonts, media and the nested scripting in PDF and SVG are historically the richest memory unsafe surface reachable without a plugin.
preconditions: a page can load the media or document type in question
oracle: the library that parses a crafted file, identified from a crash or a sandbox log
the accepted format list for a given engine version

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: GPU command and memory surface
entries.role: What a page can submit to a privileged parser, and whether GPU memory is cleared between contexts. Both are reachable without any browser exploit.
preconditions: WebGL or WebGPU available in the target context
oracle: the command set accepted and the validation applied to each
content of a fresh buffer before any write, which should be zero

tree.q: Can the factor be observed from script alone, or does it need a host view?
tree.why: The two need different instruments, and most substrate claims are made with one while needing the other.

branches.action: measure clock granularity, JIT tier thresholds and allocator reuse from inside the page
branches.oracle: a step or a discontinuity that repeats across runs

next.q: Is the target a renderer, a kernel boundary, or a native parser?

branches.action: enumerate the policy and the descriptor table, then probe reach
branches.oracle: a syscall refused at the policy and a neighbour permitted

branches.action: feed crafted inputs and identify which library parses
branches.oracle: a crash or sandbox denial naming the library

branches.action: read a fresh buffer before any write
branches.oracle: non zero content, which is a cross context read

mirror.attack: cache timing against a quantised clock
mirror.detect: timer granularity floor and jitter distribution monitored in the engine build
mirror.control: clock coarsening and jitter in the engine, per site isolation
mirror.rule: a page deriving a value from a timing difference smaller than the quantisation step

mirror.attack: renderer leak crossing an origin boundary
mirror.detect: process boundary violations and renderer crash telemetry
mirror.control: site isolation, one renderer per site
mirror.rule: a renderer reading memory belonging to another site's process

mirror.detect: allocator quarantine occupancy and reuse latency anomalies
mirror.rule: an allocation landing at a freed address inside the quarantine window

mirror.attack: reach past the sandbox after a renderer bug
mirror.detect: seccomp denials and broker message validation failures
mirror.control: sandbox policy narrowing and broker argument validation
mirror.rule: a syscall or broker call the policy should refuse

mirror.attack: reading a GPU buffer left by another context
mirror.detect: buffer initialisation audit on context creation
mirror.rule: non zero content in a buffer read before any write
